w: Rabbi Chaim Pinto lived and prayed here, on the second floor of a whitewashed courtyard building inside the old city walls of what was once Mogador. No Jewish community remains in Essaouira, but pilgrims and tour groups still fill the single-room synagogue, its ark repainted light blue.
s: Rabbi Chaim Pinto's home synagogue, still visited by pilgrims
_facts: The home and synagogue of Rabbi Chaim Pinto, on the second floor of a three-storey courtyard building inside the old city walls
No Jewish community remains in Essaouira today, but the synagogue is used when pilgrims or Jewish tour groups visit
Whitewashed plaster-over-masonry building; two women's sections, one across the courtyard, one on the third floor
Modern renovation concealed the ceiling and column capitals and painted the Torah ark and bimah light blue
